analyst_observations: Zero discriminating assertions. Both arms scored 25/25, so this eval set has no power to separate the skill from a capable baseline, and the pass rate should not be read as evidence the skill helps.
Cost is a wash again: with-skill averaged 64.6k tokens / 274.6s, baseline 66.0k / 285.6s. Both differences are inside run-to-run noise.

The classifier fix did change behaviour, which the grades cannot show. Three with-skill runs used the new 'unconfirmed' label and then verified it against the diff; one wrote 'The collector classified this as unconfirmed, not fixed-higher. That was correct.' On the pre-fix code the same data produced 'already fixed at #6115', which is false.

The baselines reached the same conclusions by reading job logs directly. On a stack of 8 PRs with 1 real failure, manual analysis is tractable, so the collector saves effort rather than changing the answer. A set that discriminates would need either a larger stack or a case where reading logs by hand is not feasible in one session.

Both arms found defects in the collector that the assertions did not ask about: skipped sharded checks are invisible to name matching, and an RSpec::Rebound retry-rescued pass is recorded as a clean pass. Both are written up in DEFECT-found-during-iteration-1.md.
